regulation: Yes. California DMV regulations govern autonomous-vehicle testing with a safety driver, driverless testing, and deployment under Title 13 of the California Code of Regulations, Division 1, Chapter 1, Articles 3.7 and 3.8.
status: Testing and deployment allowed by permit. California DMV issues permits for testing with a safety driver, driverless testing, and deployment. Vehicles must operate only within the locations, conditions, and restrictions approved in the applicable DMV permit.
committee: Senate Committee on Transportation and Housing
driver: Driverless allowed with a DMV permit. Testing with a safety driver requires the driver to be seated in the driver’s seat, monitor the vehicle, and be capable of immediately taking manual control. California also permits driverless testing and deployment when the manufacturer obtains the applicable DMV permit and satisfies the approved operating conditions. Cal. Veh. Code § 38750(b)–(e); 13 CCR arts. 3.7–3.8.
liability: Manufacturers testing or deploying autonomous vehicles must maintain $5 million in insurance, surety bond, or self-insurance under Cal. Veh. Code § 38750. No separate $5 million AV-specific requirement is imposed on an individual private owner; the owner remains subject to California’s generally applicable vehicle insurance requirements.
commercial: Allowed with regulatory approvals. A manufacturer must obtain a California DMV deployment permit to deploy autonomous vehicles on public roads. A company providing autonomous passenger transportation must also obtain the applicable authorization from the California Public Utilities Commission; paid passenger service requires participation in a CPUC deployment program.
procedure: Testing with a safety driver: apply to the DMV for a manufacturer’s testing permit, designate and train test drivers, and provide evidence of $5 million in financial responsibility. Driverless testing: obtain a DMV driverless testing permit and submit required safety, operational-design-domain, law-enforcement interaction, and financial-responsibility information. Deployment: submit the DMV deployment application, certify compliance with federal and state safety requirements, provide testing and safety information, submit a law-enforcement interaction plan, maintain $5 million in financial responsibility, register the vehicles, and operate only within the conditions approved by the DMV.

Fully autonomous commercial and motor-carrier vehicles may operate under applicable state and federal commercial-vehicle laws, except requirements applicable only to human drivers; school buses are excluded. On-demand autonomous passenger networks are expressly permitted under applicable transportation-for-hire laws. See W. Va. Code §§ 17H-1-7 and 17H-1-8.
procedure: Before operating without a human driver, submit a law-enforcement interaction plan to WVDOT under W. Va. Code §17H-1-5(b), and submit proof of insurance or self-insurance satisfactory to the DMV under §17H-1-10.

status: Automated-vehicle operation and testing are allowed only when a licensed human operator remains behind the wheel and in physical control
driver: Licensed operator must be behind the wheel and in physical control; driverless operation is not allowed
liability: No AV-specific amount
commercial: Fully driverless commercial deployment is not authorized
sources: ​​​Rules of the Road - Legal Status of CAV in Wisconsin

status: WYDOT and the Wyoming Highway Patrol maintain a voluntary reporting system for manufacturers conducting ADS vehicle testing in Wyoming. Manufacturers are asked to notify the Highway Patrol before testing, and all testing must comply with applicable state vehicle and safety-driver requirements.
